document: A coconut seller has to transport coconuts using either rickshaws or ox carts. The rickshaws can take 90 coconuts each and cost $6 per trip. The ox carts can take 20 coconuts each and cost $5 per trip. The seller has at most $100 to spend on transporting the coconuts. Due to pollution, the number of rickshaws must not exceed the number of ox carts. Formulate a LP to maximize the number of coconuts that can be transported.

integrality.note: text says LP, but trips are integer

document: A furniture store only stocks and sells dining tables and chairs. The profit per dining table is $200 and the profit per chair is $120. There is 800 sq ft of space available and a dining table requires 10 sq ft of floor space while a chair requires 3 sq ft. Because chairs sell in larger quantities, at least 50% of all furniture in the store must be chairs. In terms of capital, a dining table ties up $2000 in capital and a chair ties up $180 in capital. The company wants a maximum of $30000 worth of capital tied up at any time. Formulate an LP to maximize profit.

A bakery sells two types of cakes. They sell a chocolate cake and a vanilla cake. Let's say they make x1 chocolate cakes, at a profit of $20 each, and x2 vanilla cakes, at a profit of $13 each (x1 and x2 are unknowns both greater than or equal to 0). The daily demand for these cakes is at most 70 chocolate cakes and at most 50 vanilla cakes. The bakery is short staffed and can make a maximum of 70 cakes of either type per day. How much of each cake should the bakery make in order to maximize profit?

integrality.note: asks how much, or is about investing

document: A company wants to advertise its product. They want to use three types of ads: magazine ads, flyers, and billboard ads. The cost for each option along with the expected viewership is given. A magazine ad costs $2000 and attracts 7000 viewers. A flyer costs $300 and attracts 8000 viewers. A billboard ad costs $9000 and attracts 33000 viewers. To avoid annoying customers, the city has limited the number of flyers from a single company to 7. In addition, at most a third of the total number of ads should be billboard ads and at least 9% of the ads should be magazine ads. If the weekly budget is $40000, how many ads of each type should be run in order to maximize the number of viewers?

A spicy paste is to be made from units of peppers and tomatoes and is to contain a minimum of 170 units of spice and 50 units of flavor. Peppers cost $10 per unit and tomatoes cost $8 per unit. One unit of peppers contains 7 units of spice and 3 units of flavor. One unit of tomatoes contains 1 unit of spice and 10 units of flavor. Formulate this as an LP and find the minimum cost spicy paste that can be made.

A suit store makes 2-piece and 3-piece suits. To make a 2-piece suit requires 1 hour of measuring and 2 hours of stitching. To make a 3-piece suit requires 3 hours of measuring and 9 hours of stitching. The store has 86 hours of measuring time and 500 hours of stitching time available. In order to stay in business, at least 20 2-piece suites should be made. The profit per 2-piece suit is $800 and the profit per 3-piece suit is $900. Formulate a LP to maximize profit?

The Chips Alloy company produces 130 tons of iron ore and 36 tons of zinc ore each month. These can be treated in different ways to produce three different alloy grades: Standard, Plus or Premium. To produce 1 ton of the Standard grade alloy requires 5 tons of iron ore and 1 ton of zinc ore. To produce 1 ton of the Plus grade alloy requires 4 tons of iron ore and 3 tons of zinc ore. Finally, to produce 1 ton of the Premium grade alloy requires 10 tons of iron ore and 5 tons of zinc ore. The profit per ton from selling the alloys are $2100, $3700 and $4400 for the Standard, Plus, and Premium grades respectively. How much of each alloy grade should be produced to maximize profit?

A kitchen prepares diced onions and carrots each involving both peeling and cutting. To prepare a container of diced onions takes 7 minutes of peeling and 10 minutes of cutting. To prepare a container of diced carrots takes 10 minutes of peeling and 12 minutes of cutting. There are 3000 minutes of peeling time and 1500 minutes of cutting time available. If the profit per container of diced onions is $9 and the profit per container of diced carrots is $4, how many containers of each should be prepared to maximize profit?

A cell-phone company makes foldable and regular cell-phones in a factory that is divided into a hardware and software section. The hardware section must work 20 hours on each foldable cell-phone but only 5 hours on each regular one. The software section must work 5 hours for each cell-phone. The profit from the foldable cell-phone is $600 and the profit from the regular cell-phone is $200. Due to a recent strike, the hardware section only has 300 hours available per week and the software section only has 95 hours available per week. How many of each phone should the company produce to maximize profit?

The Vision Corporation manufactures two models of monitors: Aleph 3 and Gilgamesh Supreme. They share a similar manufacturing process in that they both require a certain amount of assembly and packaging. Each Aleph 3 monitor takes 3 hours of assembly and each Gilgamesh Supreme requires 3.0 hours of assembly. They both require 0.8 hours of packaging time per unit. During the next season, 3000 hours of assembly time are available and at most 1400 hours of packaging time may be used. Each Aleph 3 sold yields a profit of $2900. Each Gilgamesh Supreme sold yields a profit of $1400 profit. Formulate and solve this LP problem and find the best combination of monitors that yields the highest profit.

A factory in India produces rice and corn. To make one kilogram of rice requires 4 hours of human labor, 2 hours of machine work, and 7 hours of resting under the sun. To make one kilogram of corn requires 1 hour of human labor, 6 hours of machine work, and 1 hour of resting under the sun. The factory only has 60 hours of human labor, 300 hours of machine labor, and 130 hours of time under the sun available. The net profit per kilogram of rice is $10 and the net profit per kilogram of corn is $18. How many kilograms of each should the factory make in order to maximize profit?

David likes to mix his two post workout drinks: coconut water and blue energade. Coconut water costs $5 per bottle, contains 6 units of potassium, 5 units of magnesium, and 10 units of calcium. Blue energade costs $6 per bottle and contains 20 units of potassium, 3 units of magnesium, and 3 units of calcium. David likes to make sure he gets at least 26 units of potassium, 20 units of magnesium, and 30 units of calcium after each workout. How many bottles of each drink should he buy and mix in order to ensure a minimum cost? What is the minimum cost?

George has 84 acres of farmland on which to grow strawberries and watermelons Both fruits have to be watered and sprayed with bug repellant. There are 290 days per year available for watering and 90 days per year available for spraying bug spray. It takes 0.4 days to water an acre of strawberries and 1 day to spray an acre of strawberries. It takes 0.1 days to water an acre of watermelons and 3 days to spray an acre of watermelons. George earns a profit of $100 per acre of strawberries and $300 per acre of watermelons. How many acres of each fruit should be planted in order to maximize profit?

A fashion company produces two types of nail paints, gel and acrylic. The profit per unit of gel is $40 and the profit per unit of acrylic is $300. It takes 6 hours to produce the raw materials for one unit of gel, 2 hour to mix and 9 hours in packing. It takes 4 hours to produce the raw materials for one unit of acrylic, 3 hour to mix and 2.7 hours in packing. Per month, 400 hours are available for preparing the raw materials, 460 hours for mixing and 430 hours for packing the nail paints.  How many of each type of nail paint should be produced in order to maximize the total monthly profit?

Bold Tycoon wants to put his $6,000 to work and decides to invest his money in GICs and index ETF. GICs  yields a 3% return whereas index ETF yields an average return of 9.8%. To meet his long-term investment goal, he needs to place at least $2,000 in index ETF.  Nonetheless, he is risk averse and wants at least 20% of his money to be safely invested in GICs.  Help Bold Tycoon determine an asset allocation that will maximize his average return.

integrality.note: asks how much, or is about investing

document: A paint manufacturer produces 200 kg of dye and 300 kg of filler each week. By using different combinations, they can produce three different paint products for sale: Low Quality, Regular Quality, and Premium Quality. The profit per kg for selling the paint is $70, $300, $370 for the low quality, regular quality, and premium quality respectively. To produce 1 kg of low quality paint requires 9 kg of dye and 10 kg of filler. To produce 1 kg of regular quality paint requires 6 kg of dye and 6 kg of filler. To produce 1 kg of premium quality paint require 29 kg of dye and 3 kg of dye. Formulate the problem of deciding how much of each paint to make each week as a LP problem in order to maximize profit.

Two brothers, John and William, run a stand selling lemonade and brownies. A pitcher of lemonade takes 0.8 hours of John's time along with 0.1 hours of William's time. A batch of brownies take 1 hour of John's time and 0.8 hours of William's time. John has 20 hours available each day, but since William has hockey lessons, he only has 5 hours available each day. They get $10 profit per pitcher of lemonade, and $9 per batch of brownies. Formulate a LP to maximize profit.

An electronics company makes economical and premium mobile phones in a factory that is divided into a hardware and software section. The hardware section must work 4 hours on each economical mobile phone but 18 hours on each premium one. The software section must work 5 hours for each mobile phone. The profit from the economical mobile phone is $220 and the profit from the premium mobile phone is $800. Due to a recent strike, the hardware section only has 220 hours available per week and the software section only has 70 hours available per week. How many of each phone should the company produce to maximize profit?

document: A meat processing plant has a machine that makes ham and bacon. Each kg of ham takes 12 minutes of machine time and each kg of bacon takes 5 minutes of machine time.  In a week the machine is only available for 1000 minutes. The plant can also make at most 300 kg of ham and at most 350 kg of bacon per week. If the profit per kg of ham is $10 and the profit per kg of bacon is $15, how many of each should the plant make to maximize profit?

A software company has UI designers earning $1300 per week and software engineers earning $1000 per week. The contracts with companies to provide cloud services require at least 40 workers, of whom at least 20 must be software engineers. To make sure there is enough experience on the team, the number of software engineers should be at least a third of the number to UI designers. The company wants to keep the weekly wage bill below $100000. Formulate an LP problem to minimize the wage bill.

A factory makes bike tires and car tires. Bike tires take 5 minutes on the manufacturing machine and 3 minutes to fill with air. Car tires take 10 minutes on the manufacturing machine and 2.4 minutes to fill with air. The factory can run the manufacturing machine for at most 500 minutes and they have 300 minutes available for filling the tires with air. If the profit per bike tire is $6 and the profit per car tire is $30, how many of each tire should the factory make to maximize profit?

A company makes raincoats and umbrellas with images of Latin alphabet on them using a printing machine. Due to the popularity of Latin alphabet, the company must make at least 1800 raincoats or umbrellas, in any combination, per week. Also, in one week, the printing machine must be kept running for at least 100 hours. A raincoat takes 0.5 hours of printing time and costs $8. An umbrella takes 0.8 hours of printing time and costs $15. Formulate this problem so as to minimize total production costs.

A TCM company makes powdered medicine in two different packages, a regular package and premium package, to sell to TCM doctors. The regular package requires 50 g of medicinal herbs and 40 seconds of drying. A premium package requires 160 units of medicinal herbs and 80 seconds of drying. The company has available 5000 units of medicinal herbs and has available 5900 seconds in the drying machine. Since the premium package sells better, the number of regular packages must be less than the number of premium packages. In addition, the company must make at least 8 regular packages. If a regular package can treat 3 people and a premium batch can treat 5 people, how many of each type of package should be made to maximize the number of people that can be treated?

notes.detail: c2_xy: text says 'less than' (strict); modeled as <=

document: A company is delivering packages using two methods, drones and couriers. A drone can transport 6 packages every hour while a courier can transport 20 packages every hour. Drones cost an average of $3 per hour to maintain and couriers are paid $10 per hour. The company needs to deliver at least 900 packages and they can spend at most $2500 per hour for delivery. Since drones have a high up-front cost, the number of drones cannot exceed the number of couriers. How many of each method of delivering packages should be used to minimize the total number of deliveries using drones and couriers?

A vending machine supplier is purchasing vending machines and they can buy a double-load or single-load model. A double-load vending machine sells 200 items whereas a single-load machine sells 367 items. The double-load machine needs to be re-stocked five times every month and uses 20 units of electricity every month. The single-load machine needs to be re-stocked two times every month and uses 6 units of electricity every month. Since the single-load machine is smaller and easier to fit, there must be at least 6 single-load models. However, due to the storage capacity, management prefers to have twice as many double-loads than single-load machines. Further, the supplier needs to sell at least 6000 items every month, and can use at most 1000 units of electricity. How many of each vending machine type should the supplier purchase to minimize the total number of times restocked?

A university has 850 units of antibiotics to make two creams, a anti-inflammatory cream and a pain-killing cream. A container of anti-inflammatory cream requires 3 units of antibiotics and 6 units of water. A container of pain-killing cream requires 2 units of antibiotics and 3 units of water. The lab has to make at least 30 anti-inflammatory creams. However, since pain-killing creams are in high demand, at least 48% of the total number of creams must be pain-killing creams. How many of each should be made to minimize the total amount of water needed?

A florist can deliver their flowers either by car or by truck. A car can deliver 9 units of flowers and uses 7 units of gas. A truck can deliver 10 units of flowers and uses 27 units of gas. The florist needs to deliver at least 150 units of flowers. Additionally, the number of cars used must exceed the number of trucks used. How many of each should be used to minimize the total amount of gas used?

notes.detail: c1_xy: text says 'must exceed' (strict); modeled as >=

document: A nutritionist recommends that a child eat fruits and drink juice to tackle a certain disease. Each serving of fruit contains 3 units of the necessary mineral and 2 units of hydration. Each serving of juice contains 5 units of the necessary mineral and 4 units of hydration. According to the nutritionist, the child must intake at least 70 units of the necessary mineral every week and 20 units of hydration for their body to better absorb the mineral into their body. Further, each serving of fruit contains 6 units of sugar and each serving of juice contains 18 units of sugar. Since juice is more convenient, the child wants to take at least twice as many servings of juice as fruits. How many of each should the child be served to minimize the total sugar intake?

A patient lacking sleep can take two drowsiness medications, sleeping pills, and sleep supplement. Per serving, sleeping pills increase sleepiness by 4 units and introduces 0.8 units of discomfort. Per serving, sleep supplement increases sleepiness by 5.5 units and introduces 0.2 units of discomfort. Furthermore, pills contain 1 unit of sugar while sleep supplement contains 2.2 units of sugar per serving. The patient needs at least 5 units of sleepiness and can take at most 2.2 units of discomfort. How many servings of each should the patient take to minimize his sugar intake?

A fitness trainer meal-preps two types of meals, a salmon lunch and a bison burger. The salmon lunch contains 14 grams of protein, 30 grams of carbs, and 5 grams of fat. The bison burger contains 20 grams of protein, 30 grams of carbs, and 21 grams of fat. The fitness trainer wants to get at least 130 grams of protein and 110 grams of carbs. In addition, because the salmon lunch is expensive, at most 19% of the meals should be salmon lunch. How many of each meal should he eat if he wants to minimize his fat intake?

A physics class is performing a volcano experiment using two mixtures, mixture A and mixture B. Mixture A uses 2 units of baking soda, 9 units of vinegar, and produces 3 units of eruption. Mixture B uses 6 units of baking soda, 4 units of vinegar, and produces 6 units of eruption. However, mixture A generates 3 units of garbage and mixture B generates 1 unit of garbage. The physics class has available 100 units of baking soda and 200 units of vinegar. If at most 80 units of garbage can be generated, how many of each type of mixture should be used to maximize the total amount of eruption produced?

A smoothie company offers delivery and ships in specialty delivery and medium bags. A specialty delivery bag can hold 23 orders while a medium bag can hold 10 orders. Most delivery drivers prefer medium bags, so at least three times as many medium bags must be used as specialty delivery bags. The smoothie company has at most 26 medium bags and 50 specialty delivery bags. If the company must send at least 4 specialty delivery bags and can send at most 70 bags in total, how many of each should they send to maximize the total number of smoothies that can be delivered?

A lumber company owns and can use at most 700 acres of land where they can transport the lumber out using large and small logging trucks. Per acre of land, small logging trucks can be used to transport 2 units of wood. Per acre of land, a large logging truck can transport 4 units of wood. However, a small logging truck produces 14 units of carbon dioxide and requires 4 units of gasoline per acre. A large logging truck produces 15 units of carbon dioxide and requires 14 units of gasoline per acre. The lumbering company has access to 4200 units of gasoline and the company has vowed to limiting pollution to 10000 units of carbon dioxide. How should the two types of logging trucks be distributed to stay within the limits of carbon dioxide while maximizing the amount of wood transported?

An airport can transport travelers using commercial planes and private planes. A commercial plane can carry 96 travelers while a private plane can carry 50 travelers. Because the destination is more remote, there are few airport runways. Therefore, there must be twice as many private planes as commercial planes. If the airport needs to transport at least 6800 travelers, how many of each type of planes should be used to minimize the total number of planes used.

A house painting company can transport their paint in large cans or small cans. Large cans can hold 7 litres of paint while small cans can hold 3 litres of paint. Since small cans can be used up quickly and thus, not dry up as easily, the company wants to have at most 20% of the cans be large cans. However, there has to be at least 10 large cans especially for the basic colours. If the company needs to transport at least 220 litres of paint, how many of each size of cans should be transported to minimize the total number of cans?

A strawberry farmer delivers his strawberries in two types of containers, a box and a bucket. A box contains 4 units of strawberries whereas a bucket contains 8 units of strawberries. The farmer has access to 400 boxes and 500 buckets. Buckets sell for more profit; therefore, the farmer wants to sell at least three times more buckets than boxes. Additionally, he can transport at most 640 containers and at least 21 must be boxes. How many of each type of container should the farmer order to maximize the total amount of strawberries he can transport?

A supermarket can purchase two types of refrigerators to properly store their food, refrigerator ABC and refrigerator XYZ, and they have different specifications to consider. Refrigerator ABC is larger and can store 170 items but uses 2 kWh. Refrigerator XYZ is smaller more efficient and can store 100 items but uses 1 kWh. Due to soaring electric prices, the store is limited to at most 97 kWh but must store at least 2800 items. The store must have at least 10 refrigerator ABC’s and 4 refrigerator XYZ’s. How many of each type of refrigerator should the supermarket purchase to minimize the number of refrigerators needed?

An MOA checks a patient’s eye pressure one-by-one either by using a tonometer or a “puff of air” test. The tonometer test takes 0.04 hours to make a reading while the ”puff of air” test takes 0.03 hours to make a reading. Since the tonometer is more standard, the number of tonometer tests must be larger than the number of “puff of air” tests. Since a lot of these patients are low risk here for a check-up, at least 40 patients should have their eye pressure checked using the “puff of air” test. If the office is open for 5 hours, maximize the number of patients whose temperature can be taken?

document: A dental firm hires two types of employees: dentists and oral hygienists. Dentists work 10 hours every shift and oral hygienists work 4 hours every shift. Additionally, dentists are paid $500 per shift while oral hygienists are paid $150 per shift. It is close to Halloween and the dental firm expects more patients coming in. They require 800 hours of labour. There must be at least 40 shifts of dentist to keep the office running. If there is a budget of $130000, how many of each type of employee should the firm schedule to work to minimize the total number of shifts?

A milk company is delivering milk to their local families’ homes directly either through bikes or by car. A worker on a bike can deliver 13 orders of milk and takes 30 minutes per trip. A worker on a car can deliver 40 orders of milk and takes 50 minutes per trip. The milk company needs to deliver at least 430 orders of milk. Additionally, at least 50% of delivery trips must be by bike to reduce the pollution. How many of each type of delivery trips must be scheduled to minimize the minutes per trip?

A logging company ships their lumber to a nearby country using logging trucks and by lumber carrier vessels. Each logging truck costs the logging company $230 for every trip and moves 900 lbs of lumber. A lumber carrier vessel costs $900 every trip and moves 4000 lbs of lumber. Due to limited waters and difficulties in scheduling the trips for lumber carrier vessels, the company’s management asks that the number of logging trucks must exceed the number of lumber carrier vessels. The logging company must transport at least 500000 lbs of lumber to the nearby country. How many of each type of transportation should the company schedule to move their lumber to minimize the total cost?

document: A tutoring company hires full-time tutors and supplements with assistant tutors from a nearby high school. Every day, full-time tutors work 10 hours and get paid $930 while assistant tutors work 8 hours and get paid $170. During Christmas break, the tutoring company expects more interest and plans to require 1100 hours of teaching availability. If the tutoring company has a budget of $99000, how many tutors and assistant tutors should be hired to minimize the amount of staff?

A nurse suggests that his patient drink more protein shakes and milk to meet their calcium and protein requirements. One glass of protein shake contains 5 units of calcium, 3 units of protein, and 5 grams of sugar. One glass of milk contains 8 units of calcium, 1 unit of protein, and 8 grams of sugar. The patient must get at least 60 units of calcium and 150 units of protein. Since the patent prefers milk, they must drink at least 2 times as many glasses of milk as glasses of protein shakes. How many glasses of each should they drink to minimize their sugar intake?

A food distributer can either move their product using trucks or boats. A truck can take 40 units of product and produces 90 units of pollution per trip whereas boats take 60 units of product and produces 100 units of pollution per trip. The food distributer needs to move 600 units of product and must have a maximum of 30% of the trips using boats due to limitations of sea transportation regulations. Additionally, there must be at least 5 trips using a truck. How many of each form of transportation should be used to minimize the total amount of pollution produced?

A physics teacher shows her students two experiments, a force experiment and a hydraulics experiment. In the force experiment, 4 units of the solid and 3 units of the gas mixes and reacts to create 5 units of excitement. In the hydraulics experiment, 9 units of the solid and 10 units of the gas mixes and reacts to create 4 units of excitement. In addition, the hydraulics experiment produces 3 units of heat while the force experiment produces 5 units of heat.  The lab has available 100 units of the solid and 54 units of the gas. If at most 11 units of heat can be produced, how many experiments of each should be done to maximize the total excitement?

An athlete drinks protein shakes in the morning before a workout and is planning for the coming month. She has two selections of protein shakes, chocolate powder or vanilla powder shakes. Each scoop of chocolate powder protein shake contains 10 grams of protein and 5 grams of sugar. Each scoop of vanilla powder protein shake contains 24 grams of protein and 4 grams of sugar. Since she prefers the vanilla flavour, she would like to drink at least twice as many vanilla powder shakes as chocolate powder shakes. However, she must also drink at least 3 scoops of the chocolate powder shake. To avoid high blood glucose levels, she is limiting her consumption to at most 400 grams of sugar over this period of time. How many of each protein shake should the athlete drink to maximize her total protein intake over this period of time?

A sample can be analyzed by two machines for their chemical make-up, Analyzer 3000 and QuickAnalytics. Analyzer 3000 analyzes 40 samples of water and 20 samples of dirt per hour. QuickAnalytics examines 30 samples of water and 8 samples of dirt per hour. In addition, Analyzer 3000 creates 1.8 units of heat per hour while QuickAnalytics creates 3.9 units of heat per hour. If at least 600 samples of water and 1000 samples of dirt must be analyzed, how many hours should each machine be used to minimize the total amount of heat produced?

A university has a car building fundraiser where students build toy cars and toy trucks using wheels and wood and sell to benefit a nearby shelter. A toy car requires 3 wheels and 10 units of wood while a toy truck requires 7 wheels and 6 units of wood. Each team has at most 70 wheels and 52 units of wood. In addition, each team can build at most 4 toy cars and the number of toy trucks must be larger than the number toy cars. If a toy car can fundraise $60 and a toy truck can fundraise $69, how many of each toy should a team build to maximize the total amount fundraised?

document: Architects ABC has a budget of one hundred thousand dollars to spend every week on their employees. They hire architects and drafters to help with their clients’ projects. An architect averages 4000 dollars every week and can complete 3 projects every week. A drafter does not have all the certifications and requires an architect for supervision at all times. Therefore, there must be more architects than drafters. Additionally, a drafter averages 670 dollars every week and completes 1 project every week. How many architects and drafters should be contracted to maximize the number of projects completed every week?

document: A manufacturing plant has the option to offer a shuttle bus and outsource to a taxi service. A shuttle bus costs $30 and carries 9 workers, whereas a taxi service costs $40 and carries 3 workers. The manufacturing plant has to transport at least 450 workers and at most 3 shuttle buses can be used. How many of each type of transport should be taken to minimize the total cost?

A government sanitization plant processes liquid waste and solid waste in batches. Liquid waste requires 20 units of disinfectant and 10 units of bacteria. Solid waste requires 31 units of disinfectant and 21 units of bacteria. The sanitization plant has available 1200 units of disinfectant and 900 units of bacteria. The batches of liquid waste processed must be twice the number of solid waste processed. In addition, at most 7 batches of solid waste can be processed due to storage limitations. If each liquid waste batch is the result of 7 people and each solid waste batch is the result of 2 people, how many of each should the plant process to maximize the number of people served?

A researcher is transporting their arsenal of imaging systems using two different methods, by delivery truck and by van. Transporting by delivery truck takes 8 hours and costs $500 per trip. Transporting by van takes 6 hours and costs $100 per trip. The researcher needs to transport 10 trips worth of equipment and has a budget of $9400. Additionally, the number of transports by the delivery truck must be less than the number of transports by van. How many of each transportation method should they use to minimize the total number of hours spent on delivery?

document: A butcher sells marinated wild boar and processed lamb chops. Each portion of marinated wild boar requires 2 minutes of preparation and 9 ounces of meat. One portion of processed lamb chops requires 1 minute of preparation and 5 ounces of meat. Since processed lamb chops are more popular and common, the butcher plans to make at least twice as many processed lamb chops as marinated wild boars. The butcher has a small staff and only has available 340 collective minutes every week to preparing these two items and only has available 2410 ounces of meat. If a portion of marinated wild boar sells for a revenue of 9 dollars whereas a portion of processed lamb chops sells for a revenue of 3 dollars, how many of each should the butcher make to maximize their revenue?

A water purification station has a large plant and a small plant. The large plant purifies 20 units of water per hour and produces 40 units of by-product per hour. The small plant purifies 11 units of water per hour and produces 3 units of by-product per hour. The large plant requires 16 filters while the small plant requires 11 filters per hour. The water purification station only has available 1000 filters right now. If the station must purify at least 1000 units of water and at least 300 units of by-product, how many hours should each plant be run to minimize the total time needed?

A clothing manufacturing company needs to transport their product by cargo ship or airplane. A cargo ship can transport 70 units per trip while by airplane can transport 50 units per trip. A cargo ship produces 10 units of pollution and an airplane produces 21 units of pollution. There can be at least 3 airplane trips made and at least 48% of all trips must be made by cargo ship. The company needs to transport at least 720 units of their product. How many of each transportation should they use to minimize the total amount of pollution produced?

A garbage collection company uses two types of vehicles, truck A and truck B. Truck A requires 6 workers while truck B requires 7 workers. Truck A can collect 50 units of garbage and truck B can collect 100 units of garbage. The garbage collection company has employed 200 workers. The company must use more truck A models than truck B models. Additionally, there must be at least 9 truck A’s and 10 truck B’s. How many of each type of vehicles should the company use to maximize the total amount of garbage that can be collected?

A landscaping company provides services from an expert or an apprentice. An expert costs the company 800 dollars for each shift and can care for 50 square meters of land whereas an apprentice costs the company 500 dollars for each shift and can care for 40 square meters of land. Because of the price to the customer, the company expects the demand of the public to want at least twice as many apprentices than experts. However, there are loyal customers that prefer the experts. Therefore, at least 20% of shifts must be expert shifts. The company must care for 7000 square meters of land. How many of each type of service should be used to minimize the total cost to the company?

A doctor can prescribe two types of medication for high glucose levels, a diabetic pill and a diabetic shot. Per dose, diabetic pill delivers 1 unit of glucose reducing medicine and 4 units of blood pressure reducing medicine. Per dose, a diabetic shot delivers 4 units of glucose reducing medicine and 2 units of blood pressure reducing medicine. In addition, diabetic pills provide 0.5 units of stress and the diabetic shot provides 0.6 units of stress. At most 10 units of stress can be applied over a week and the doctor must deliver at least 20 units of glucose reducing medicine. How many doses of each should be delivered to maximize the amount of blood pressure reducing medicine delivaered to the patient?

There are two methods of extracting a chemical element, method X and method Y.  Method X requires 7 atomic units (au) of aluminum, 1 au of oxygen, and can extract 0.4 au of the desired chemical element. Method Y requires 10 au of aluminum, 3 au of oxygen, and can extract 0.5 au of the desired chemical element. There are 1100 au of aluminum, and 231 au of oxygen available. What is the best combination of these two methods to maximize the total amount of desired chemical element?

A toy storage company needs to transport toys using a manual pallet jack or an electric pallet jack. The toy storage company has access to at most 5 manual pallet jacks and 9 electric pallet jacks. The manual pallet jacks can transport 9 boxes every hour while electric pallet jacks can transport 14 boxes every hour. Since electric jacks require less work, the number of electric pallet jacks must exceed the number of manual pallet jacks. If the company can use at most 10 manual pallet jacks and at least 6 electric pallet jacks, how many of each should the company use to maximize the number of boxes they can transport?

notes.detail: c0_xy: text says 'must exceed' (strict); modeled as >=

document: A composting company can store compost in medium containers and large containers. A medium container needs to be checked 6 times a week and can store 19 units of compost. A large container needs to be checked 4 times a week and can store 30 units of compost. The company needs to store at least 700 units of compost and there must be at least 2 medium containers. There must also be at least 4 large containers and the number of large containers must be three times as much as the number of medium containers. How many of each type of containers should be used to minimize the total number of times checking containers?

A chemist is performing novel research to create element A using two known methods: the gamma experiment and the omega experiment. The gamma experiment creates 11 units of element A and uses 5 units of electricity, 10 units of copper, and 5 minutes. The omega experiment creates 18 units of element A and uses 3 units of electricity, 6 units of copper, and 1 minutes. The chemist has available 900 minutes, 6700 units of copper, and 2100 units of electricity. How many of each experiment should the chemist perform to maximize the total amount of element A produced?

A strawberry farmer has available 323 hectares of land and she needs to harvest the strawberries either through employees or U-pick. For each hectare of land, employees can hand-pick 100 lbs of strawberries which creates 7 lbs of waste, and takes 20 minutes. Conversely, for each hectare of land, opening the farm for U-pick can pick 35 lbs of strawberries which creates 40 lbs of waste, but only takes 40 minutes. The farmer has a maximum amount of people allowed on the field at all times and due to the restriction of trying to sell the product while it is still fresh, expects that at maximum capacity she only has 6000 minutes available for picking. Additionally, there can be at most 7600 lbs of waste. How many hectares should be allocated to each harvesting technique to maximize the amount of strawberries that can be picked?

A pharmaceutical manufacturing plant has 2000 mg of cornstarch to rush orders of diabetic pills and latex gloves. Each diabetic pill requires 5 mg of cornstarch and 0.3 minutes to manufacture. Each individual latex glove requires 10 mg of cornstarch and 0.28 minutes to manufacture. The pharmaceutical manufacturing plant needs to make at least 40 diabetic pills. Since latex gloves are important, at least 80% of produced items must be latex gloves. How many of each should the pharmaceutical manufacturing plant make to minimize the total number of minutes needed?

A woman with vitamin deficiency is taking supplements from two brands, super vitamin XYZ and vitamin ABC. Super vitamin XYZ contains 3 mg of vitamin, 4 mg of fiber, and causes 3 units of drowsiness per serving. Vitamin ABC contains 2.9 mg of vitamin, 2 mg of fiber, and causes 2 units of drowsiness per serving. The woman wants to get at least 20 mg of vitamin and 46 mg of fiber. In addition, there must be at most 30% of the supplements taken from super vitamin XYZ and there must be at least 2 servings of super vitamin XYZ because it is expiring soon. How many servings of each should she take to minimize her total drowsiness.

An internet supplier needs to deliver routers to their customers when they first sign up. They can either transport using their internal drivers or outsource to external drivers. Internal drivers spend more time to help the customers set up and can deliver 40 routers every day whereas the external drivers can deliver 19 routers every day. External drivers use hybrid cars and produce 6 units of pollution while the internal drivers use gasoline cars and produce 18 units of pollution. The internet supplier needs to deliver at least 700 routers every day and internal drivers must make up at least 10% of all drivers due to their customer service. There must also be at least 6 external drivers. How many of each type of driver should the internet supplier plan to contract to minimize the total amount of pollution?

Emergency supplies need to be delivered to a remote area and can either go by airplane or helicopter. An airplane can transport 38 units of goods and takes 20 minutes while a helicopter can transport 30 units of goods and takes 5 minutes due to easier take-off and landing. The number of helicopters must exceed the number of airplanes. Additionally, there must be at least 8 airplanes to fully utilize the landing space.  If there needs to be at least 600 units of goods transported, how many of each type of transportation should be utilized to minimize the total number of minutes needed?

document: A hospital gives pupil dilation drops using two types of dilation drops, fast-acting eye drops and slow-acting eye drops. The fast-acting eye drops take 3 minutes per patient to adjust the patient’s pupils while the slow-acting eye drops take 43 minutes per patient. Since the fast-acting eye drops are more expensive, at least twice as many patients must be dilated using the slow-acting eye drops than the fast-acting eye drops. However, at least 43 patients must be dilated with the fast-acting eye drops. If the clinic is open for 18000 minutes, maximize the number of patients that can be dilated.

A famous chocolate shop is expecting a lot of orders because of an upcoming holiday. The chocolate shop is famous for selling two products, large boxes of chocolates, or small boxes of chocolates. A large box of chocolate has 36 individual chocolates while a small box of chocolate has 19 individual chocolates. The chocolate shop has a delivery service, and each trip, the shop owner can prepare ahead of time at most 120 large boxes of chocolates or 110 small boxes of chocolates. Due to space limitations of their truck, the truck can fit at most 70 total boxes of chocolates and because of a sale, there must be at least 5 large boxes of chocolates. However, small boxes of chocolates are less expensive and the shop owner expects to move at least three times as many small boxes of chocolates than large boxes of chocolates. How many of each size of chocolate box should the shop owner put in their truck for each trip to maximize the total number of individual chocolates transported to their customers?

A competitive swimmer is training heavily and to do so, plans to eat steaks and chicken breasts over the coming week. Each steak contains 1000 calories and 70 g of protein. Each chicken breast contains 600 calories and 10 g of protein. He prefers to eat chicken breasts and decides to eat at least 3 times as many chicken breasts as steaks over the coming week. However, he must also eat at least 20 steaks over the week. If he must consume at least 1600 g of protein over this coming week, how many steaks and chicken breasts should he eat to minimize the total amount of calories he is eating?

A nearby lake is frequently artificially seeded with trout for local fishermen. The trout are transported using either large trucks or by boat. Transporting using large trucks can take 3000 trout and costs $400 per trip. Transporting with boat can take 1900 trout and costs $200 per trip. Since boats take extra preparation, at least 91% of trips should be by large trucks. Additionally, there can be at most 8 trips by boat. If at least 10000 trout need to be seeded into the nearby lake, how many of each type of trip should be taken to minimize the total cost?

In the North, a delivery service can deliver using either sleds or snowmobile. Snowmobiles can deliver 79 packages while sleds can deliver 100 packages. Most villages do not want snowmobiles to pollute their regions. Therefore, there must be at least two times more sleds than snowmobiles. If the delivery service wants to deliver 170000 packages, minimize the total number of deliveries.

A waste treatment company must remove waste using a large container or a medium container. A large container can take 7 tons of waste while a medium container can take 2.2 tons of waste. The treatment plant has available at most 50 large containers and 39 medium containers. Additionally, due to logistics in the storage warehouse, there must be at most 78 total containers and they must use at least 4 medium containers. Finally, there must be twice as many medium containers than large containers. How many of each container should they use to maximize the total amount of waste they can transport?

A car manufacturing company needs to distribute their cars to their retail stores by either large trailers or small trailers. A large trailer can carry 10 cars while a small trailer can carry 2 cars. Since large trailers are harder to get a hold of, the number of small trailers used has to be at least three times the number of large trailers used. If at least 100 cars need to be transported, minimize the total number of trailers needed.

A gas company can transport gas using a pipeline or by train. A pipeline can carry 10000 units of gas and a train can carry 1000 units of gas every day. Due to recent environmental changes, the number of trains used must be at least twice as many as the number of pipelines. If at least 800000 units of gas needs to be transported every day, minimize the total number of pipelines and trains needed.

An ice cream company sells ice cream as cones and tubs. A cone of ice cream contains 6 oz of ice cream while a tub contains 12 oz of ice cream.  Due to the recent wave of heat and a recent promotion, the company expects to sell at least 4 times more cones than tubs of ice cream. However, to reduce labour time and looking at previous sales, management decided to require stores to at least create 60 tubs of ice cream. If the company has the capacity to make 4000 oz of ice cream, how many orders of each should be made to maximize the total number of sales of ice cream?

A commercial fishing company has available 400 square kilometers of water that they can fish from. They can either allocate a square kilometer for fish farming or trawling. For each square kilometer of ocean, fish farming causes 5 units of pollution and nets 2 tons of fish and requires 10 workers every day. For each square kilometer of ocean, trawling causes 20 units of pollution, nets 6 tons of fish and requires 3 workers every day. Due to environmental regulations, there must be at most 1100 units of pollution and the company has available 300 workers daily. Find the proportion of lands that use each fishing technique to maximize the daily yield of fish.

A chemical company makes an acidic liquid and a basic liquid using two types of techniques, reaction X and reaction Y. Reaction X can make 47 au of the acidic liquid and 71 au of the basic liquid per minute. Reaction Y can make 36 au of the acidic liquid and 47 au of the basic liquid per minute. Furthermore, reaction X requires 13 units of heat every minute while reaction Y requires 11 units of heat every minute. The chemical company has the capacity to generate at most 1200 units of heat every minute. If the chemical company needs to make at least 500 au of the acidic liquid and 1100 au of the basic liquid per minute, how many minutes should each reaction be run for to minimize the total time needed?

integrality.note: asks how many minutes each reaction runs

document: A construction site can use two transfer methods to move equipment using cranes or elevators. Each crane can transport 10 units of equipment and costs $3000 per hour. Each elevator can transport 3 units of equipment and costs $1000 per hour. The construction site needs to transport at least 50 units of equipment and has available $40000. There must be at least three times more elevators than cranes. How many of each type of transfer method should be done to minimize the total number of transfer methods?

notes.detail: objective 'total number of transfer methods' lists no variables; used their sum

document: An engineering kids kit has two sets, a mechanical and chemistry kit. The mechanical kit requires 3 units of plastic, 2 units of materials and entertains a kid for 2 hours. The chemistry kit requires 4 units of plastic, 10 units of materials and entertains a kid for 3 hours. The chemistry kit however produces 5 units of waste while the mechanical kit produces 9 units of waste. The company has available 800 units of plastic and 530 units of materials. If the company has committed to producing at most 200 units of waste, how many of each type of kit should the company make to maximize the number of hours of entertainment?

An extremely large mall needs at least 50 transportation methods for customers to move up and down floors. They can either purchase an escalator or an elevator. Due to space limitations, there must be more escalators than elevators, but for convenience, there must be at least 5 elevators. An elevator can transport 500 customers every day and uses 9 units of electricity in that time span. An escalator can transport 3000 customers every day and uses 10 units of electricity in that time span. The mall has available 1000 units of electricity every day. How many of each transportation method should the mall install to maximize the number of customers they can transport every day?

A fitness trainer is scheduling her client to eat more fruits and vegetables to meet their vitamin and fiber requirements. A pack of fruits contains 3 units of vitamin and 12.0 units of fiber. A pack of vegetables contains 5 units of vitamin and 8 units of fiber. The client must meet their weekly minimum requirements of 60 units of vitamin and 180 units of fiber. In addition, because fruits contain more hydration, the client must eat at least twice as many packs of fruits as packs of vegetables. If a pack of fruits contains 2 units of sugar and a pack of vegetables contains 1 unit of sugar, how many of packs of each should the client consume to minimize their sugar intake?

A skiing resort has two methods of getting their customers up to their resort. They can either use a gondola, or a large bus. On average, a gondola can transport skiers and snowboarders at a rate of 40 people per minute whereas a large bus can transport at a rate of 7 people per minute. However, gondolas cost the resort a lot to maintain and at most 50% of the transportation methods implemented can be gondolas. Since large buses are easier to implement, there must be at least ten times more large buses than gondolas. If the manufacturer wants to move at least 400 customers every minute up the mountain, find the minimum transportation implementations that can be used.

A dietician recommends his patient drink more juice and vitamin-added milk to increase her vitamin and hydration intake. Each cup of juice contains 23 units of vitamins and 5 units of hydration. Each vitamin-added milk contains 7 units of vitamins and 20 units of hydration. The patient needs to consume at least 210 units of vitamins and 100 units of hydration. Since the patient is slightly lactose-intolerant, there must be at most 20% of all cups of drinks be vitamin-added milk. If each cup of vitamin-added milk contains 4 units of sugar and each cup of juice contains 20 units of sugar, how many cups of each should she drink to minimize her sugar intake?

A restaurant chain can make two types of meals, a steak or vegetarian meal. The steak meal makes $29 profit each and it takes 2 minutes for a chef to make. A vegetarian meal makes $10 profit each and takes 3 minutes for a chef make. The restaurant chain needs to make at least $400 profit every day and has available 2000 minutes of chef involvement. How many of each meal should the restaurant try to push through the waiting staff to minimize the total number of meals they need to make?
